what: Two rear drives propel the rover while a third motor turns its front bogie. A/B drive; C steers the front bogie within ±20°. Free front half-shafts allow different wheel speeds. Compare pivot steering with Ackermann geometry.
try: Reset and run both programmed curves.
Watch the front axle angle separately from the rear wheel speeds.
Stop, use a small manual steering angle and then drive gently.
why: The angled front bogie guides the chassis while the rear wheels provide traction. This is wagon-style steering rather than an ideal Ackermann linkage.
matters: Mechanical steering and differential wheel-speed steering solve the same navigation task differently.
question: If the steering angle changes sign, what should happen to the curve?
answer: At the same forward drive direction, the curve changes side. Reversing travel also reverses the relation between heading change and displacement.
